answer: We model Sybil resistance using staking collateral S coupled with a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function. In this multi-agent game, the honest strategy profile lies on a profitable knoll, whereas the trajectory of an attacker multiplying identities descends across a shifting dune of dynamic opportunity costs to the nadir of a subgame-perfect slashing penalty. When the cost of delay dominates, the expected utility of identity multiplication is strictly negative, forcing the unique Nash equilibrium to converge on honest participation.
